text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOHA JONE
- The newspaper editorial says the opposition Socialist Party's campaign ahead of October 20 local elections has been less effective than the ruling Democrats' campaign.
- Two police stations in Tirana received hoax bomb warnings by telephone.
- A report on forthcoming local elections, compiled by 153 Italian observers, will be independent of the Council of Europe, which is organising international monitoring of the poll.
- U.S. embassy staff visited two northern towns to meet political parties before local elections.
- Albanian embassy staffing will change significantly after the local elections.
- Ethnic Albanians from Kosovo held a rally in front of Bonn's interior ministry to oppose the return of refugees to their homes in the former Yugoslavia.
- Alleged poisonings of Albanian children in Macedonian schools has created a tense situation.
- Albania and Turkey pledged to increase sea and air transport between the two countries.
- Some 2,700 Albanians have won a U.S. green card, allowing them to go and live there.
- Albania's Vefa and Germany's Platter have opened a sausage factory.
- A polio immunisation programme continued as more people were taken ill and disputes began about the availibility of vaccine.
- A Tirana ship is being blocked in a Turkish port following a disagreement over payments. Turkey's Orion Shipmanagement Industry and Trade says it is owed $700,000 by the Albanian Trade Fleet.
GAZETA SHQIPTARE
- The Independent Trade Union said it may stage a two-day strike after local elections in protest at rising bread and fuel prices.
RILINDJA DEMOKRATIKE
- Tritan Shehu, deputy Prime Minister, Foreign Minister and chairman of the Democratic Party, met Britain's John Major and other British ministers who pledged support for Albania.
ZERI I POPULLIT
- The opposition Socialists have claimed that voting lists have been manipulated by the ruling party. They claim the names of thousands of people who are dead or absent appear on the lists.
